name: Questions to Ask Before Letting an ADU Contractor Alter Your Roof or Second Story

mainEntity.name: What should I ask an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County before cutting into my existing roof or second story?
mainEntity.text: What should I ask an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County before cutting into my existing roof or second story?

acceptedAnswer.text: When planning an ADU addition that modifies your roofline or second story in Los Angeles County, you need to vet contractors beyond a standard remodeling checklist. Ask how they coordinate with a licensed structural engineer and whether structural drawings are included in their price. Clarify how they will verify existing framing sizes, spans, and connections before demolition, and what happens if hidden conditions differ from original plans. Request a step‑by‑step weather protection plan: temporary roofing, tarps, staging, and how they handle unexpected rain once your roof is open. Have them explain exactly how the new loads from the ADU will be carried down to the foundation, and whether any retrofit or new footings are anticipated. Ask for photos and addresses of at least two past projects where they altered a roof or added a second‑story or over‑garage ADU. Discuss noise, debris, and safety controls for occupants, including working hours and dust barriers. Finally, review how change orders are triggered, how often you’ll receive progress updates, and what inspection milestones the city will require. Contractors who can clearly explain these items, in writing, with specific examples are more likely to manage the risks and complexity of cutting into your existing structure for an ADU addition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before allowing an ADU additions contractor to cut into an existing roof or second story in Los Angeles County, ask about their structural engineering process, how they’ll protect the home from weather, how they’ll handle tie‑ins to existing framing, their experience with similar additions, and what contingencies they include for hidden conditions.
